body:
Ideally `git-repository` users won't ever have the need to pull in a plumbing crate directly. Thus `git_sec` should be `git::sec` here unless it's a matter of preference.

The reason for that is that they will only have to maintain one crate version to use anything `git` related, which is `git-repository`. Note that as per [gitoxide's stability policy](https://github.com/Byron/gitoxide/blob/498072ea42dca7b9d00bedba42829bdac92195b9/STABILITY.md#L1-L0) breaking changes in exposed dependencies of `git-repository` will automatically lead to a breaking semver change in `git-repository` transitively, so doing so should be preferred and is save to do as well.
Is this not fixed in `gitoxide` by now? I thought it won't over-eagerly make paths relative anymore.

There is a [`head_commit()`](https://github.com/Byron/gitoxide/blob/b362fb594546400e6c42688103df438954df7eeb/git-repository/src/repository/reference.rs#L213) method now.

Generally, `gitoxide` wants to make common tasks simple, and I am happy to add what's seemingly missing, too.
There is a [`head_id()`](https://github.com/Byron/gitoxide/blob/b362fb594546400e6c42688103df438954df7eeb/git-repository/src/repository/reference.rs#L194) method as well.
Thanks, I didn't notice that this was included in `git-repository`.
Thanks, I hadn't updated that yet.

I thought I would be a good idea to handle repo trust with some basic checks, though it might be better to wait until `secure.directories` can be handled to improve the experience. At this time, (our) starship builds with git2 don't handle this at all.
I've used `debug` over `warn` here to make this less noisy.

I see, it's probably preferable to fail gracefully than have `git` bail out, even though with the current implementation I bet `starship` would be over-eagerly bailing even though `git` might be configured to accept the path.

I don't know if using `git config` to obtain the `safe.directories` value is feasible in the meantime (or does that bail out too :D?)

This is mostly intended as a fallback in case git hasn't yet been updated to use a security model.

Using `git config` might slow down the prompt too much on Windows (#2888).

Actually I was wrong about this, and the way it's currently implemented this value is overridden by the trust level that was determined anyway rendering the `with(…)` adjustment ineffective.

For a moment I was about to neuter the implementation to not be so strict and all in the name of saving a permission check which right now isn't proven to save any perceivable time. All this resulted in [this commit](https://github.com/Byron/gitoxide/commit/270242c707bd086b7746ee45b55791587f1484b1) to add more information on the security implications.

For starship this means it will definitely not accidentally cause the execution of a binary controlled by an attacker, now or in the future, which I think is desirable.

That said, once actual performance measurements of the cost of the permission check (probably mostly on windows) are available, it might be worth reviewing this stance. For now I think it's good to start on the safe side.
Ok, I've removed the line. Is `git::Permissions::all()` likely to become an issue? I noticed it includes some DoS protections, which might even be desirable in trusted repos.
